title: Partitioning beta diversity
text: beta_decay() adds distance sites along gradient. turnover rises elevational distance nestedness stays low.  beta_decay_model() fits distance-decay curve similarities (one minus dissimilarity) tests . exponential model S = exp(-b d) gives similarity sites elevation rate b; half_distance elevational distance similarity halves. Pairs sites share sites, independent: p-value comes permuting site labels, Mantel test, refitting model time. five sites per season 120 distinct permutations, smallest attainable p-value near 0.01 however strong pattern.

what: Hill-number dissimilarity between pairs of sites
title: Partitioning beta diversity
text: Presence-absence indices treat species one worker like one thousand. beta_hill_pair() computes Hill-number framework Chao, Chiu Jost (2014) every pair sites, order q sets much weight common species get. q = 0 dis_sorensen dis_jaccard classic Sorensen Jaccard indices; q = 2 dis_sorensen Morisita-Horn index, driven dominant species.  beta_dist() turns one order distance matrix ordination, clustering PERMANOVA:

what: Beta diversity at equal sample coverage
title: Partitioning beta diversity
text: Beta diversity estimated samples depends sample size completeness, regions sampled different effort compared directly. beta_hill() follows iNEXT.beta3D framework Chao et al. (2023): gamma alpha Hill numbers standardised sample coverage, beta = gamma / alpha effective number completely distinct sites (1 number sites). four dis_ columns rescale beta 0-1. dis_sorensen dis_jaccard measure non-overlap (q = 0 classic Sorensen Jaccard dissimilarities); turnover versions measure species turnover. Give coverage compare regions chosen levels: Add nboot bootstrap confidence intervals. function gives phylogenetic (type = "PD", tree) functional (type = "FD", distance) beta diversity, works incidence data unit sampling units (plots, visits) surveyed every site. Chao, . et al. (2023). Rarefaction extrapolation beta diversity framework Hill numbers: iNEXT.beta3D standardization. Ecological Monographs, 93, e1588.
code: beta_hill(png_ants, .by = season) #> # A tibble: 6 × 13 #>   season     q coverage m_gamma m_alpha gamma alpha  beta n_sites dis_sorensen #>   <chr>  <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>   <int>        <dbl> #> 1 dry        0    0.957    238.    371.  50.3 16.2   3.10       5        0.526 #> 2 dry        1    0.957    238.    371.  34.1 10.9   3.12       5        0.708 #> 3 dry        2    0.957    238.    371.  24.7  7.32  3.37       5        0.879 #> 4 wet        0    0.957    480     807.  78.9 27.9   2.83       5        0.457 #> 5 wet        1    0.957    480     807.  39.4 13.6   2.89       5        0.659 #> 6 wet        2    0.957    480     807.  22.2  7.29  3.04       5        0.839 #> # ℹ 3 more variables: dis_jaccard <dbl>, dis_turnover_sorensen <dbl>, #> #   dis_turnover_jaccard <dbl> beta_hill(png_ants, q = 0, coverage = c(0.8, 0.9), .by = season) #> # A tibble: 4 × 13 #>   season     q coverage m_gamma m_alpha gamma alpha  beta n_sites dis_sorensen #>   <chr>  <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>   <int>        <dbl> #> 1 dry        0      0.8    81.9    140.  34.5  11.5  3.01       5        0.503 #> 2 dry        0      0.9   150.     244.  44.4  14.5  3.06       5        0.516 #> 3 wet        0      0.8   112.     216.  43.3  15.9  2.73       5        0.433 #> 4 wet        0      0.9   260.     481.  64.1  23.5  2.73       5        0.431 #> # ℹ 3 more variables: dis_jaccard <dbl>, dis_turnover_sorensen <dbl>, #> #   dis_turnover_jaccard <dbl> set.seed(1) b <- beta_hill(png_ants, q = 0, coverage = 0.9, nboot = 20, .by = season) b[c("season", "beta", "beta_lower", "beta_upper")] #> # A tibble: 2 × 4 #>   season  beta beta_lower beta_upper #>   <chr>  <dbl>      <dbl>      <dbl> #> 1 dry     3.06       2.56       3.57 #> 2 wet     2.73       1.97       3.48

title: Testing community composition
text: term tested (= "margin", default), result depend order terms formula. design balanced, sequential tests (= "terms", vegan’s default) give numbers; correlated terms . Elevation explains 17% variation composition (Bray-Curtis). test season respecting paired design, permute within sites: season effect, hidden large differences elevations, becomes clear transect compared transects site.

title: Testing community composition
text: PERMANOVA can also give significant result groups differ spread rather location (Anderson 2006). Check :  seasons similar dispersion, season effect real shift composition, difference spread. dispersions differ, group sizes unbalanced, use Welch-type PERMANOVA W*d (Hamidi et al. 2019), stays valid unequal spread:
code: disp <- beta_dispersion(ants, site = unit, group = season) attr(disp, "test") #> # A tibble: 2 × 5 #>   term         df  sum_sq statistic p.value #>   <chr>     <int>   <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl> #> 1 Groups        1 0.00182     0.466   0.501 #> 2 Residuals    18 0.0702     NA      NA autoplot(disp) set.seed(1) beta_welch(ants, site = unit, group = season) #> # A tibble: 1 × 4 #>   statistic n_groups n_sites p.value #>       <dbl>    <int>   <int>   <dbl> #> 1      1.29        2      20   0.179

title: 2. Hill numbers, completeness and coverage
text: Diversity combines two things: many species (richness) evenly individuals spread among . forest 10 species, one making 91 % trees, feels less diverse one 10 equally common species. Classic indices (Shannon H′, Simpson D) capture incompatible scales: doubling species double H′. Hill numbers (Hill 1973) solve . Hill number order qq qD=(∑=1Spiq)1/(1−q) ^{q}D = \left( \sum_{=1}^{S} p_i^{\,q} \right)^{1/(1-q)} pip_i relative abundance species ii SS number species. effective number species: number equally common species give diversity. Hill numbers units species, community twice many equally common species exactly twice diversity (“replication principle”; Jost 2006; Chao et al. 2014). code: # A site with one species has a zero standard error and no weight shannon <- filter(est, q == 1, !is.na(weight)) fit_lm <- lm(estimate ~ elevation + I(elevation^2) + season,   data = shannon, weights = weight ) broom::tidy(fit_lm, conf.int = TRUE) #> # A tibble: 4 × 7 #>   term              estimate  std.error statistic p.value    conf.low  conf.high #>   <chr>                <dbl>      <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>       <dbl>      <dbl> #> 1 (Intercept)     8.61       2.23           3.87  0.00830  3.16          1.41e+1 #> 2 elevation      -0.00557    0.00376       -1.48  0.189   -0.0148        3.63e-3 #> 3 I(elevation^2)  0.00000117 0.00000154     0.760 0.476   -0.00000260    4.95e-6 #> 4 seasonwet       2.42       1.72           1.40  0.210   -1.80          6.64e+0 fit_mm <- lme4::lmer(estimate ~ elevation + season + (1 | site),   data = shannon, weights = weight / mean(weight) ) summary(fit_mm)$coefficients #>                 Estimate  Std. Error   t value #> (Intercept)  8.335239972 1.936638262  4.303974 #> elevation   -0.002897246 0.001183797 -2.447418 #> seasonwet    2.126186442 1.391201962  1.528309 fit_gam <- mgcv::gam(estimate ~ s(elevation, k = 4) + season,   data = shannon, weights = weight / mean(weight), method = "REML" ) summary(fit_gam)$s.table #>                  edf  Ref.df        F    p-value #> s(elevation) 1.00008 1.00016 8.487165 0.02254615 grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(   elevation = seq(200, 2200, by = 20),   season = c("wet", "dry") ) pred <- predict(fit_gam, grid, se.fit = TRUE) grid$fit <- pred$fit grid$se <- pred$se.fit ggplot(grid, aes(elevation, fit, colour = season, fill = season)) +   geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = fit - 1.96 * se, ymax = fit + 1.96 * se),     alpha = 0.2, colour = NA   ) +   geom_line() +   geom_pointrange(aes(y = estimate, ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high),     data = shannon   ) +   scale_colour_tidydiversity() +   scale_fill_tidydiversity() +   labs(     x = "Elevation (m)",     y = "Shannon diversity (effective number of species)",     colour = NULL, fill = NULL   ) +   theme_tidydiversity() rich <- filter(est, q == 0, !is.na(weight)) broom::tidy(glm(estimate ~ elevation + season,   data = rich,   family = Gamma(link = "log"), weights = weight / mean(weight) )) #> # A tibble: 3 × 5 #>   term         estimate std.error statistic p.value #>   <chr>           <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl> #> 1 (Intercept)  2.10      0.440         4.78 0.00200 #> 2 elevation   -0.000597  0.000259     -2.31 0.0544  #> 3 seasonwet    0.822     0.498         1.65 0.143 obs <- div_hill(png_ants, q = 0, .by = season) |> add_site_data(sites) broom::tidy(glm(diversity ~ elevation + season + offset(log(n)),   data = obs, family = poisson )) #> # A tibble: 3 × 5 #>   term          estimate std.error statistic    p.value #>   <chr>            <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>      <dbl> #> 1 (Intercept) -0.874      0.181       -4.81  0.00000148 #> 2 elevation    0.0000230  0.000131     0.175 0.861      #> 3 seasonwet   -0.197      0.173       -1.14  0.256

text: beta_decay() gives one row per pair sites distance along one gradients. Several columns give Euclidean distance. Pairs independent, test relationship Mantel test rather lm p-values.
code: decay <- beta_decay(png_ants, elevation, .by = season) broom::tidy(lm(turnover ~ distance + season, data = decay)) #> # A tibble: 3 × 5 #>   term         estimate std.error statistic      p.value #>   <chr>           <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>        <dbl> #> 1 (Intercept)  0.664    0.0723        9.18  0.0000000531 #> 2 distance     0.000168 0.0000590     2.85  0.0110       #> 3 seasonwet   -0.0149   0.0590       -0.252 0.804 wet <- filter(png_ants, season == "wet") d_beta <- beta_dist(beta_pair(wet), "turnover") d_elev <- dist(distinct(wet, site, elevation)$elevation) vegan::mantel(d_beta, d_elev, permutations = 999) #> 'nperm' >= set of all permutations: complete enumeration. #> Set of permutations < 'minperm'. code: library(ggplot2) data(list = c(   "Brazil_rainforest_abun_data", "Brazil_rainforest_phylo_tree",   "Brazil_rainforest_distance_matrix" ), package = "iNEXT.3D") wide <- Brazil_rainforest_abun_data brazil <- tibble(   site = rep(colnames(wide), each = nrow(wide)),   species = rep(rownames(wide), ncol(wide)),   n = unlist(wide, use.names = FALSE) ) |>   filter(n > 0)  curves <- bind_rows(   div_rarefy(brazil, abundance = n, type = "TD") |> mutate(type = "TD"),   div_rarefy(brazil,     abundance = n, type = "PD",     tree = Brazil_rainforest_phylo_tree   ),   div_rarefy(brazil,     abundance = n, type = "FD",     distance = as.matrix(Brazil_rainforest_distance_matrix)   ) )  curves$type <- factor(curves$type, levels = c("TD", "PD", "FD"))  ggplot(curves, aes(m, diversity, colour = site)) +   geom_line(aes(linetype = method == "extrapolation")) +   geom_point(data = filter(curves, method == "observed"), size = 2) +   facet_wrap(vars(q, type),     ncol = 3, scales = "free_y",     labeller = labeller(q = function(x) paste("q =", x), .multi_line = FALSE)   ) +   scale_linetype_manual(values = c("solid", "dashed"), guide = "none") +   labs(     x = "Number of individuals",     y = "Effective number of species", colour = NULL   ) +   theme_tidydiversity()

what: ForestGEO-style stem and tree census verbs — stems
title: ForestGEO-style stem and tree census verbs — stems
text: Tidyverse-style helpers ForestGEO / CTFS plot inventories. accept data frames usual columns (plot, census, treeID, stemID, gx, gy, dbh, species / sp, status, optionally date) return tibbles. Callers stay inside tidydiversity instead using fgeo CTFS packages. Typical workflow: standardise names stems_as_trees() (main stem per tree) keep stems; summarise stems_abundance() stems_basal_area(); size classes stems_size_class(); demography two censuses stems_demography(); feed species counts div_hill() via stems_as_community(). Spatial stem verbs (quadrats, habitat joins, neighbourhoods, torus-translation habitat test) stem maps topography companion package tidymapr (tidymapr::stems_quadrat(), tidymapr::stems_habitat_test(), tidymapr::plot_topo()). Basal area one stem \eqn{\pi/4 \times \mathrm{dbh}^2} (Condit 1998; fgeo.analyze). dbh_unit = "cm" result cm\(^2\); "mm" mm\(^2\). Convert afterwards need m\(^2\) ha\(^{-1}\).

title: ForestGEO-style stem and tree census verbs — stems
code: stems_as_trees(data, hom = NULL)  stems_abundance(   data,   .by = NULL,   alive_only = TRUE,   alive = "A",   level = c("tree", "stem") )  stems_basal_area(   data,   .by = NULL,   dbh_unit = c("mm", "cm"),   alive_only = TRUE,   alive = "A" )  stems_size_class(   data,   breaks = c(10, 20, 50, 100, Inf),   labels = NULL,   dbh_unit = c("mm", "cm"),   .by = NULL,   alive_only = TRUE,   alive = "A" )  stems_demography(   census1,   census2,   mindbh = 0,   alive = "A",   time = NULL,   growth = c("absolute", "relative"),   dbh_unit = c("mm", "cm"),   .by = NULL )  stems_as_community(   data,   site = NULL,   alive_only = TRUE,   alive = "A",   level = c("tree", "stem") )

NULL, estimated date columns present, otherwise required. growth "absolute" (dbh2-dbh1)/time "relative" (log dbh2 - log dbh1)/time. site Column use site identifier community table (default quadrat, added tidymapr::stems_quadrat(), plot).
